model: Hammer Strength IL-ROW, plate-loaded standard horizontal row; excludes high/low/D.Y./MTS variants

manufacturer.note: Independent workarms. Added plates are not handle-force measurements. Do not infer a stack-row or barbell conversion from these specifications.

reference.source: Stronger public iso-lateral row machine table
reference.method: Copy the displayed pound values verbatim, including their rounded bodyweight labels; interpolate between rows and clamp at endpoints. The source kg and lb displays are not exact conversions due to rounding. Beginner means below the Novice threshold; no beginner threshold was invented.
reference.limitations: The source claims population-level data without identifying a model-specific sample, sample size, grip, range of motion, loading convention or starting-resistance treatment. These are provisional family-level tiers, not validated Hammer Strength norms or percentile anchors.
reference.siteLoadConvention: Combined load including both 12 lb workarms; 70 lb plates per arm = 164 lb combined. This is an explicit local assumption because the reference convention is unspecified. The site neither doubles the logged load nor adds starting resistance again.
reference.presentation: Provisional tier + ordinal progress line, never population percentile. No percentile-based weakness signal from these tiers in recommendations. Rep targets invert the site's existing Brzycki/Epley equation.

reviewedAlternatives.decision: Not reused for IL-ROW: 307206 generic machine-row lift entries mix machine designs and unspecified conventions.
Rejected as model-specific norm: publisher explicitly states that stack and plate-loaded machines are mixed.
2006 thesis abstract reports 31 trained men and higher Hammer Strength than free-weight 1RM; it supplies no IL-ROW population tiers. Full text returned 403, so no conversion equation was used.
